cases.name: RandomForest classification with temporal CV
cases.input: Train a RandomForest classifier on our temporal dataset with proper cross-validation.
expected_behaviors: Uses TimeSeriesSplit or custom temporal splitter instead of random KFold
Encodes categorical features before passing to RandomForest
Sets random_state for reproducibility
Logs metrics to MLflow
Serializes model with joblib
should_not: Use random KFold on temporal data
Pass raw categorical columns to RandomForest
Use n_jobs=-1 without considering Azure ML compute size

cases.name: GradientBoosting regression with log-transformed target
cases.input: Train a GradientBoosting regressor on a log-transformed target variable.
expected_behaviors: Trains on np.log1p(target) as specified
Inverts predictions with np.expm1() before computing metrics
Clips negative predictions to small positive value after inversion
Reports metrics on original scale (not log scale)
should_not: Compute MAE/R2 on log-transformed predictions without inverting
Leave negative predictions uncorrected after expm1 inversion

cases.name: HistGradientBoosting with native categorical support
cases.input: Train a HistGradientBoosting model that has categorical features.
expected_behaviors: Uses categorical_features parameter to handle categoricals natively
Does NOT pre-encode categoricals (HistGradientBoosting handles them)
Does NOT require feature scaling
should_not: One-hot encode categoricals before HistGradientBoosting (wastes memory)
Apply StandardScaler (not needed for tree-based models)

cases.name: Model serialization for inference pipeline
cases.input: Save the trained sklearn model and preprocessing artifacts for the inference pipeline.
expected_behaviors: Uses joblib.dump() for model serialization
Saves preprocessing artifacts (scalers, encoders) separately
Logs artifacts to MLflow
Provides clear file paths for inference_model.py to load
should_not: Forget to save preprocessing state alongside the model
Hardcode file paths — use output_dir argument

cases.name: SVM on large dataset warning
cases.input: Train an SVM model on a dataset with 500K rows.
expected_behaviors: Warns that SVM scales poorly beyond ~100K rows
Suggests LinearSVC as an alternative for large datasets
Suggests tree-based models (RandomForest, GradientBoosting) as alternatives
If proceeding with SVM, recommends feature selection to reduce dimensionality
should_not: Silently train a standard SVC on 500K rows without warning
Recommend SVC for large datasets without caveats
